```{r}
library("here")
library(tidyverse)
rds_files <- c("b_lyrics.RDS", "ts_lyrics.RDS", "sales.RDS")
## Check whether we have all 3 files
if (any(!file.exists(here("data", rds_files)))) {
    ## If we don't, then download the data
    b_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/beyonce_lyrics.csv")
    ts_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/taylor_swift_lyrics.csv")
    sales <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/sales.csv")

    ## Then save the data objects to RDS files
    saveRDS(b_lyrics, file = here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(ts_lyrics, file = here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(sales, file = here("data", "sales.RDS"))
}

b_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
ts_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
sales <- readRDS(here("data", "sales.RDS"))
```

# Part 1: Explore album sales

## Part 1A

```{r}
sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(released = mdy(str_replace(released,"\\(.*\\]","")),
         country = fct_collapse(
           as.factor(country),
           FRA = c("FR","FRA"),
           WW = c("World","WW")),
         sales = sales/1000000
         )%>%
  filter(country %in% c("UK","US","WW"))
sales

```

## Part 1B

```{r}
sales%>%
  filter(country == "US")%>%
  mutate(years_since_release = round(time_length(interval(released, today()), "years")))%>%
  group_by(artist)%>%
  summarize(
    most_recent_album = min(years_since_release),
    oldest_album = max(years_since_release),
    median_years_since_album = median(years_since_release)
  )
```

## Part 1C
In each of the subsections below that ask you to create a plot, you must create a title, subtitle, x-axis label, and y-axis label with units where applicable. For example, if your axis says “sales” as an axis label, change it to “sales (in millions)”.
```{r}
library(scales)
sales %>%
  group_by(artist, country)%>%
  summarize(
    total_album_sales = sum(sales)
  )%>%
  ungroup()%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = artist, y = total_album_sales, fill = country))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position="fill")+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent)+
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Album Sales from each Country",
    subtitle = "Both Beyonce and Taylor Swift get most of their album \n sales from outside the USA and the UK.",
    x = "Artist",
    y = "Percent of Album Sales"
  )
```

## Part 1D

```{r}
sales%>%
  filter(country == "WW")%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sales, y = fct_reorder(title,sales), fill = artist))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")+
  labs(
    title = "Beyonce and Taylor Swift's Total Album Sales",
    subtitle = "Taylor Swift's Fearless has the greatest total album sales.",
    x = "Sales(in millions)",
    y = "Album",
    fill = "Artist"
  )
```

## Part 1E

```{r}
sales%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = released, y = sales, color = artist))+
  geom_point()+
  facet_grid(country ~ .)+
  labs(
    title = "Album Sales by Release Date",
    subtitle = "Taylor Swift's and Beyonce's albums have similar sales in the UK and world wide.",
    x = "Time of Initial Album Release (Year)",
    y = "Sales (in millions)",
    color = "Artist"
  )
```
